title: Income Tax Rules: Capital Gains on US Entity Transfer Not Taxable in India
description: The Delhi Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) has ruled that capital gains from the transfer of a US entity by an Irish company are not taxable in India. Thi.

faq.q: What is a Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA)?
faq.a: A DTAA is a tax treaty between two countries designed to prevent taxpayers from paying taxes on the same income twice – once in their country of residence and once in the country where the income is earned. It allocates taxing rights between the two countries.

faq.q: How does a DTAA impact capital gains on foreign assets?
faq.a: DTAAs typically have specific articles (like Article 13) that determine which country has the right to tax capital gains arising from the sale of various types of assets. This can mean that gains are taxable only in the resident country of the seller, or in the country where the asset is located, depending on the treaty.

faq.q: Does this ruling mean all foreign capital gains are tax-free in India?
faq.a: No, this ruling is specific to the facts of the FireEye Ireland case and the India-Ireland DTAA. The taxability of foreign capital gains in India depends on your residency status, the nature of the asset, the country involved, and the specific DTAA provisions applicable.

faq.q: Is it mandatory for NRIs to disclose foreign assets to Indian tax authorities?
faq.a: Yes, Indian tax residents, including those who become residents after a period as an NRI, are required to disclose foreign assets in their Income Tax Returns (ITR) if their income exceeds certain thresholds. NRIs generally have different disclosure requirements, but transparency is key.

faq.q: Where can I find official information on India's DTAAs?
faq.a: Official information on India's Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements can be found on the Income Tax Department's official website, incometax.gov.in, under the "International Taxation" section.
